profile.name: Komal Kumari
profile.title: Product Manager
profile.tagline: Product manager turning customer insights into measurable product outcomes.
profile.bio:
I like to start where a problem actually lives: in customer conversations, in the funnel, and in the small frictions people have stopped noticing. Over three and a half years I've taken products from the first interview to the first release, and I care as much about what we choose not to build as what we ship.

At QuantumLeap I proposed and scoped an internal CRM, held back AI features to protect a 90-day deadline, and then watched the numbers: booked-call attendance rose from 65 to 92 in a hundred, and lead-to-sale conversion from 16% to 26%, alongside the changes we made. Before that, about sixty prospect conversations revealed a pricing mismatch, and a smaller, sharper offer became thirty paid pilots in forty-five days.

More recently I've been building on my own: taking Shyne, a women's wellness app, from sixteen user interviews to a Play Store launch in about four months, and writing honest case studies on products I use every day. I do my best work with clear trade-offs, small pieces of real evidence, and teammates who would rather talk it through.

principles.title: Start with people
principles.body: Interviews and funnels first, features second. The problem usually looks different up close.

principles.title: Be honest about the evidence
principles.body: I say what I know, what I'm guessing, and what hasn't been measured yet.

principles.title: Protect the deadline
principles.body: Scope is a decision. I defer what can wait so the first release is one people can use.

principles.title: Measure what matters
principles.body: Pick a north-star, then set guardrails so a win in one place doesn't cost trust somewhere else.

projects.title: Google Photos: Memory Trail
projects.subtitle: Product Discovery · AI-Native MVP
projects.description: Users often remember a moment but not its date, place or details, and stall when the first search fails. Using public-review analysis, a 31-response survey, six task-based interviews and live retrieval replays, I framed the core problem as recovery after a failed first search, then designed Memory Trail: an AI-native concept that keeps clues and near-matches so users narrow results without starting over. In a three-user seeded test, all three recovered their target after the first attempt failed; this is directional evidence, not proof of improved retrieval in real libraries.

main.alt: Memory Trail overview: five steps from starting a search to confirming the photo, with the mechanism behind the MVP

sub.alt: Memory Trail results screen on a phone

projects.title: Blinkit: Contextual Category Discovery
projects.subtitle: Product Strategy · Growth & Experimentation
projects.description: Frequent Blinkit shoppers keep buying the same familiar items and rarely explore new categories. I studied the existing discovery surfaces and the friction behind repeat-purchase behaviour, then proposed an AI-powered contextual add-on: it infers the shopper's likely mission from their basket, recommends one relevant item with a clear reason, and lets them accept or ignore it without slowing checkout. The success framework pairs a north-star metric (share of eligible checkouts where a new-category item is bought) with guardrails on checkout time, cart abandonment and relevance.

main.alt: AI-powered contextual add-on for Blinkit: core workflow, key highlights and MVP principle

sub.alt: Blinkit checkout screen with a single suggested add-on

projects.title: Myntra: Wishlist Conversion
projects.subtitle: Product Discovery · AI-Powered Product Development
projects.description: High-intent Myntra shoppers save several products for one need, then stall because the comparison is spread across product pages. I combined an AI analysis of 2,055 public conversations with a 20-person survey and 6 interviews to find the root cause, then proposed Help Me Choose: a Wishlist workspace that resolves a 2–4 item shortlist around the shopper's own priorities, with no discounts. The case study covers prioritization, a metrics hierarchy with guardrails, and an experiment plan; no results are claimed.

main.alt: Help Me Choose overview: shortlist, diagnose, resolve and act, with the research behind it

sub.alt: Help Me Choose screen with purchase context and priorities

projects.title: Subspace.money
projects.subtitle: Product Teardown · May 2026
projects.description: End-to-end teardown of a consumer fintech app — analysed onboarding flow, payment UX, and post-transaction trust failures across the full user journey. Diagnosed UX trust breakdown (blank post-payment screen, unlabelled wallet deduction) and recommended tiered fixes prioritized by sprint capacity before GTM.

main.alt: Subspace.money app home screen showing gift card categories and trending subscriptions

highlights: Led Shyne, a consumer wellness app, from 16 user interviews to a three-feature MVP and Play Store launch in ~4 months; reached ~160 downloads, 120 registrations and 100 onboarding completions.

Used Mixpanel feature-usage patterns and qualitative feedback to refine cycle-day flexibility and add manual mood journaling; advised two other early-stage AI products on segmentation, UX and validation.

experience.role: Product Manager — CRM, Payments & Revenue Systems
highlights: Product ownership: Proposed the CRM, mapped cross-functional operations and independently owned V1 scope, feature decisions and trade-offs within approved budget and timeline. Prioritized ~25 requirements for 28 internal users.

Prioritization & execution: Deferred AI integration to protect cost and the 90-day V1 deadline; partnered with design and engineering on lead lifecycle, roles, attribution, payments and dashboards. Led UAT and rollout; retired spreadsheets within ~5 weeks.

Funnel analytics: Used SQL and funnel analysis to isolate booked-call no-shows; introduced qualification, pre-sales calls and automated reminders. Attendance improved from 65/100 to 92/100 booked calls across before/after periods (no control group).

Conversion & collections: Lead-to-sale conversion increased from 16% to 26% across observed monthly cohorts after CRM and follow-up changes. Defined credit pre-qualification, lender handoffs and repayment states; cash collected increased from ~35% to ~70% of contract value alongside financing and follow-up changes.

Financial workflows & AI: Specified GST/TDS-aware invoicing and finance handoffs, reducing turnaround from ~7 days to 1 day. Subsequently introduced OpenAI-assisted lead scoring and pre-call guidance using a 14-question intake and ~1,000 historical transcripts.

Synthesized ~60 prospect conversations to identify a scope-price mismatch in an Rs.8–12L flagship; shaped a focused Rs.3L offer for smaller service businesses. Evaluated willingness to pay, alternatives and delivery costs; acquired ~30 paid pilots in 45 days and scaled to ~10 monthly sales (Rs.30L/month).
Selected an off-the-shelf LMS over a custom build to validate demand with limited engineering investment; considered segment fit and cannibalization when packaging the offer.

experience.role: Project Manager — Customer Discovery & Funnel Operations
highlights: Coordinated customer purchase journeys and surfaced recurring objections, affordability constraints and decision friction that informed later CRM, qualification and monetization workflows.
